basis: Authorizes ONLY the zero-shot scoring job b5-arm2-score-arm1-cvcm2-2026-001 ($1.60 worst case, 3,600 s ceiling), one of THREE step-3 jobs (base, arm1, icmp15-base; $4.80 worst case against the $6.40 step cap). It decodes the SERVING Arm-1 export (b5-universal-arm1-2026-005, export/model.pt sha c6604a68; 7 languages, no Cameroonian language) over the pinned cvcm2 decode manifest (14,652 rows, sha 66c757f0, VersionId go2QA274Vd2eDm.zpgNn7_1vx2mvgc.k), built from curated version cvcm2 (46,632 rows, COMPLETE sha b206f505) whose splits come from the committed scripts/build_cameroon_pilot_splits.py unchanged. PREREGISTERED DESCRIPTIVE READING (no gate, nothing promotable): tone-sensitive CER (asr-eval-norm-v3-tone-sensitive, pooled over characters) is primary, WER secondary, reported per language and surface: cv_test (the frozen speaker+prompt-disjoint holdout, 3-6 speakers), cv_all (test + dev + <=20 train clips per train speaker, 199 of 204 speakers) and soreva (single male speaker; for eto, nmg and bkh SOREVA uses a different spelling system, so CV and SOREVA are not comparable there). Speaker-clustered 95% intervals only where a surface has >= 5 speakers. Paired model differences on identical clips: arm1-minus-base and icmp15-minus-base. Stated hypotheses, descriptive only: H1 Arm-1 (trained on Nigerian Pidgin) reads Cameroonian Pidgin (wes) better than base; H2 the 15-language pilot helps close relatives of its trained languages (bbj, fmp: East Bamileke with byv; bax: Mbam-Nkam with byv/nnh/nla; eto: A70 with ewo; bkh: A40 with bas) more than unrelated ones (fub, mua). Labels per language on cv_all CER for the best model: < 10 near-usable zero-shot, 10-25 adaptation candidate, > 25 needs data - labels, not decisions. 'Unseen' means not in any MedZen adaptation run; pretraining exposure of the base model is unknown (Meta lists training hours for some of these codes). One attempt per job, no retry, no follow-on run, no serving change; Arm-1 keeps serving.
